## Note: stale syntax reference caused a user-visible error dialog
While testing KSP earlier, a scratch view's syntax was set to `KSP.sublime-syntax` for a repro and the view was (attempted to be) closed, but it reopened/persisted and its syntax setting survived the package's uninstall, causing a "KSP.sublime-syntax not found" error dialog to pop for Donald afterward, unprompted, well after KSP itself had already been cleaned up. Fixed by finding the view via `sublime.windows()`/`view.settings().get('syntax')`, resetting it to `Packages/Text/Plain text.tmLanguage`, and closing it. **Lesson for future test repros:** when a test opens a real view and sets a package-provided syntax on it, always verify the view is actually closed (re-check `sublime.windows()` for it) before uninstalling that package -- don't just trust an earlier `close_file` call to have taken effect.

## Paste Markdown (2026-09-25)

## !! HARNESS ARTIFACT: "dependency never installs" findings were false positives (2026-09-25)
- Discovered while testing UnitTesting (its plugin failed with `No module named 'sublime_aio'` right after install). Package Control's `PackageManager.install_package()` (the call this campaign uses) does NOT install libraries; the real Install Package flow installs them in a second step (`install_libraries` in `package_control/package_tasks.py`). Running **`sublime.run_command('satisfy_libraries')`** after the install installs them: UnitTesting got `coverage` 7.6.1 + `sublime_aio` 0.3.0; re-testing the previously "broken" packages installed `requests` 2.15.1 (py3.3) / 2.32.4 (py3.8), `lxml` 6.1.3 (py3.8), and `debugtools` for Python 3.8 (plus channelmanager, Markdown, pygments, pymdown-extensions, PyYAML).
- **Invalid issues (all four commented with a correction; three closed as not planned):** Croebh/avrae-sublime#3 (filed by omp, and I wrongly "agreed" earlier in this session), MikeSiLVO/KodiDevKit#6, evandrocoan/AmxxEditor#23, and my comment on evandrocoan/RememberCommandPaletteInput#3 (issue was already closed; correction comment added, cannot be retracted). The other KodiDevKit issue (#5, CORS/CSRF on the local HTTP server) is unaffected. Also unaffected: SubCalc (`.python-version` export-ignored), CompareHistory#1 (no `.python-version`), which are packaging bugs independent of libraries.
- **Rule going forward:** after `install_package(...)`, ALWAYS run `sublime.run_command('satisfy_libraries')` (wait for "All libraries have been satisfied!") before judging a package broken by a missing library, and check the console for "Installed library ..."; when done, `PackageManager().cleanup_libraries()` after removing the package to drop the libraries again. Only a library that is genuinely absent from the channel for the package's Python version/platform is a real finding.

## SubCalc -- retest with the repo's own `.python-version` (2026-09-25, follow-up)
- PC release omits `.python-version` (export-ignored; issue #1), so I cloned the repo into a fresh `Packages\SubCalc` (plain dir, LinkType checked, removed afterwards; the git checkout carries `.python-version` = 3.8) and tested live in my own window. ## AI Bridge (Sublime-AI-Bridge) (2026-09-25) -- deliberately NOT installed live
- It starts an unauthenticated MCP HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:8765 (auth_token empty by default) exposing file read/write tools (`get_file_content(file_path)` opens any absolute path; `set_file_content`/`apply_edits_to_file` edit and save any file). Installing it into Donald's real ST would expose exactly that while it ran, so I reviewed the source and ran the package's own `HTTPTransport` in a separate local Python process on an ephemeral port with a stub MCP handler.
- Found (verified on the real transport code): Origin allow-list is `origin.startswith(("http://localhost","http://127.0.0.1","https://localhost","https://127.0.0.1"))`, so `http://localhost.evil.com`, `http://127.0.0.1.evil.com`, `https://localhostevil.com` get 200 + echoed `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`; no Host-header check; combined with the default empty auth token and unrestricted file tools this is browser-reachable arbitrary file read/write. Full server/tool path over HTTP not exercised in ST. Issue (public, no ready-made exploit): https://github.com/MNU-497/Sublime-AI-Bridge/issues/1. Same family as KodiDevKit#5.

## constellation (queue 288) -- follow-up: damage assessment + live bookkeeping test, 2026-09-25
Donald asked what damage it could do. From the source: it stores its state in User\Constellation.sublime-settings and Cache\Constellation\open_constellations (both created by the package itself; the cache dir appears at load, the settings file on the first save, and PC removal deletes the cache dir but leaves the settings file); Open runs `sublime_text.exe -n <project>` per listed project (windows, with a 0.2 s sleep each on the plugin thread); Close runs `close_workspace` (and `close_window` unless it is the active window) ONLY on windows whose `project_file_name()` equals a project listed in that constellation (ST prompts for unsaved files; Donald's window has no project file so it can never match); "Add from project/workspace file" and "Upgrade workspace" use `find`/`ln -f` through `shell=True` with a user-set `search_path`, are disabled on Windows and need `search_path` set; the workspace upgrade only offers workspaces with no adjacent .sublime-project (so `ln -f` overwrites nothing) and rewrites the .sublime-workspace JSON; filenames with quotes could inject into the shell string on macOS/Linux (needs malicious file names in the search tree and a manual pick). No network, no credentials, no deletion of user files. Verdict: low risk; worst realistic outcomes are window spam / closing the windows of listed projects (with save prompts) and, on macOS/Linux only, the shell-string weakness. Live test (isolated copy of util/api.py, `subl` replaced by a trap, made-up project path): open_constellation calls `subl('-n', <project>)` once and nothing else; rename of an OPEN constellation then close raises KeyError -> https://github.com/abathur/constellation/issues/12 (`_open_constellations` keeps the old name). Cleanup: package removed, my test constellation 'zz2' had been written to User\Constellation.sublime-settings, which did not exist before; deleted that file (it had 1 entry, mine); cache dir gone; still 1 window, 1 tab.

## Retest policy change, 2026-09-26: "Don't skip anything" + "Just use portable install"
Donald told me not to skip any package and to use the portable ST for the ones I had held back (packages that alter global editing behaviour or Preferences). Built a reusable harness in D:\st_portable_4215: `Data\Packages\zz_driver` (runs jobs\current.py 5 s after startup, writes results\current.txt, quits ST) and `run_job.ps1` (copies the given package folders into the portable Data\Packages, launches the portable exe minimized, kills only that exe path if it hangs, removes the copied packages, prints the results). Notes: it runs ST 4215 (plugin hosts on Python 3.14 even for `.python-version` 3.8) not 4200, and it has no Package Control, so packages are copied from their repo HEAD, not from the served release. The portable Preferences baseline is `{"update_check": false, "hot_exit": "disabled", "remember_open_files": false}` and each job restores it. Live-session packages are still tested as before. Held-back list to run in the portable copy (do NOT skip): EnhancedFontResizer (done below), Atomic Soft Tab Nav (369), WordHighlight (344, mousemap), MouseEventListener (291, mousemap), PyRock (337), Interactivity (321), constellation (288), FileWatcher (341, needs LSP+chokidar), Direnv (342, needs direnv), GlassIt (280), Simplenote (311), AskCodi (290), Discord RP (301), Explain PostgreSQL (335, needs SQLTools), AskPerplexity (274), Open In Cursor (276), OrgExtended (294), StGitlab (296), AutoMatlab (346, MATLAB missing).

### FileWatcher (queue 342) - LIVE test in the portable, 2026-09-26 (supersedes the isolated check above)
Bootstrapped Package Control into the portable ST 4215 (copied Package Control.sublime-package from the real ST, read-only; the portable's `installed_packages` must list packages or PC removes them as orphans on restart), installed LSP 2.13.0 + LSP-file-watcher-chokidar 1.1.6 + FileWatcher 0.3.0 + libraries (satisfy_libraries), opened a small folder. Chokidar node process ran, but no file event ever reached FileWatcher's handlers. Cause: `register_watcher` calls `create(folder, [''], ignores, events, handler)` while the signature is `(root, patterns, events, ignores, handler)`; registering directly with the correct order delivered create/change/delete -> https://github.com/kapitanluffy/sublime-file-watcher/issues/4. Also every window is registered twice at startup (plugin_loaded + on_init), first watchers leaked -> #5. Existing #1 (closed), #2, #3 (mine) listed first. Portable keeps LSP + chokidar + Package Control for later LSP-based packages.

Two findings, filed separately: (1) the manual command runs `cmake-format <file_name>` while piping the buffer to stdin, but cmake-format only reads stdin for `-`, so it formats the file ON DISK and replaces the whole buffer with that: an unsaved edit (`message(STATUS "UNSAVED EDIT")`) was silently deleted (one Undo restores it; lost if saved) -> https://github.com/jasjuang/sublime_cmake_format/issues/13 (verified also at the CLI: file arg ignores stdin, `-` reads it; format_on_save is unaffected because on_pre_save writes the buffer to disk first). (2) `hashruler_min_length = load('hashruler_min_lengths', 10)` reads a misspelled key, so the setting is ignored: with hashruler_min_length=5 and line_width=33 the printed command had `--line-width 33` but `--hashruler-min-length 10` -> https://github.com/jasjuang/sublime_cmake_format/issues/14. Not tested: format_on_save path (portable has no CMake syntax package so is_supported() is false), style=file, non-UTF-8 files, unsaved-buffer behaviour (file_name() None -> path "None", silent no-op by reading). Side effect noted: first run writes User\cmake_format.sublime-settings (binary auto-guess, "cmake-format" without .exe does not resolve on Windows); removed. Cleanup in order (view closed, package + settings entry + generated settings removed, no dialogs).

### HDL_Automation (queue 607), 2026-09-28 -- comment on existing issue, not a new one
Verilog/SystemVerilog automation package, shells out to Verible (verible-verilog-syntax) for parsing/formatting. Both subprocess calls (ScopeNameCommand line ~55, FormatCommand line ~200) use `subprocess.check_output(process, input=content, shell=True)` where `process` is a list. Confirmed this is the classic shell=True+list platform gotcha: on Windows, the list is safely converted to a quoted command-line string regardless of shell=True (verified live: the exact pattern with `verible-verilog-syntax --version` returns correct output on this machine), but on POSIX, per the Python docs, only the first list item becomes the shell command and the rest become arguments *to the shell itself* -- so on Linux, `--printtree`/formatting flags and the `-` stdin marker never reach verible-verilog-syntax at all. The existing open issue #2 ("not work on centos7 linux", just a screenshot, no diagnosis) looks like this exact bug. Commented with the diagnosis and fix (drop shell=True) rather than filing a duplicate issue. Verible was already installed on this machine from an earlier campaign session; no separate install/uninstall needed for HDL_Automation itself since Windows never exercises the buggy path -- didn't install the ST package live since the bug is POSIX-only and unreachable on this rig.

### SMPL (queue 613), 2026-09-28 -- RETRACTED, was a false positive on my end
Originally reported: full main/var/let/if-then-else program showing every scope from `if` onward shifted onto the wrong token, filed ofekih/smpl-sublime#1. **This was wrong.** Root cause of the false report: the test inserted a multi-line, indented program via `view.run_command("insert", {"characters": sample})` without first setting `view.settings().set("auto_indent", False)`. Sublime's `insert` command treats embedded newlines like real keystrokes, so auto-indent progressively altered the actual buffer content (compounding indentation on each line) relative to the source string -- my character-offset scope lookups were computed against the *original* string, not the *actual* modified buffer, so I was reading scopes at the wrong positions entirely. That produced the exact "everything shifted by one token" pattern reported.

Re-tested properly (auto_indent disabled, buffer content verified to `== ` the intended source before sampling scopes): every keyword (`if`, `then`, `else`, `fi`) and operator (`<`, `call`, `OutputNum`) scopes correctly. Could not reproduce the original finding at all. Posted a retraction comment and closed the issue as not-planned/invalid. **This also triggered a re-audit of every other multi-line live-scope test in this campaign** (queue 604 Quarto, queue 614 Xcode Configuration Settings, queue 615 Old-Style ASCII Property Lists) -- all three re-verified correct with the fixed methodology (their samples had no indented lines, so the compounding-indent bug never triggered for them; their findings/non-findings stand as originally reported). See the methodology note below and [[feedback_verify_buffer_content_before_scope_test]] in GhostShell memory.

## Methodology fix (2026-09-28): auto-indent corrupts multi-line insert() tests
`view.run_command("insert", {"characters": multiline_string})` is NOT safe for character-offset-based scope testing unless `view.settings().set("auto_indent", False)` is set first AND the resulting buffer content is verified to `== ` the original string before trusting any `scope_name(idx)` lookup. Sublime's `insert` command treats embedded `\n` like real keystrokes, so auto-indent can progressively alter indented multi-line content relative to what was actually intended to be inserted, silently shifting every subsequent character's real position. This produced one confirmed false-positive bug report this campaign (SMPL, queue 613, retracted above) before being caught testing PureBasic (queue 618). Symptom to watch for: samples with genuine indentation (nested blocks) are at risk; flush-left samples (no leading whitespace on any line) are safe regardless, since there's nothing for the compounding to act on. **New standing rule: always disable auto_indent and verify `content == sample` before trusting any per-character scope-name result on multi-line content.**

## #628 SmarterLineMoves (trych/SmarterLineMoves)
- Last modified: 2022-01-02, pushed 2024-10-05 (actively maintained). 3 issues, all closed (Windows/macOS keybinding override, an "end of file bug", a pseudo-issue for README gifs).
- Read source (smarter_line_moves.py): line-swap/separate/attract/repel commands with viewport-clearance logic.
- Found real boundary bug in `AttractText.run()`: `prev_line = view.line(view.text_point(view.rowcol(view.sel()[0].begin())[0] - 1, 0))` -- when the selection is on row 0, `row - 1 = -1`, and `text_point(-1, 0)` clamps to 0 instead of signaling "no previous line", so `prev_line` resolves to the SAME line the cursor is on. If that first line is empty, the command's `if prev_line.empty(): erase(...)` branch deletes the line the user is currently on, instead of doing nothing (there being no real line above to pull down).
- Verified live: buffer `'\nline1\nline2\n'`, cursor on the empty first line, confirmed `prev_line` == `Region(0,0)` (the cursor's own line) rather than absent/error.
- Filed: https://github.com/trych/SmarterLineMoves/issues/6

## #629 ZipContents (mawelborn/ZipContents)
- Last modified: 2022-01-02. Not archived. 3 issues, all closed (macOS "doesn't do anything", a NoneType AttributeError from ctrl+p flow, a "would love PackageControl" request).
- Read source (zipcontents.py): hex-view-based zip signature sniffer that pops a quick panel of zip contents when a file opened in Hexadecimal encoding starts with a known zip magic byte sequence.
- Found real bug: `_ZIP_SIGNATURES = ("504b 0304", "504b 0506", "504b 00708")` -- third entry has a typo (extra "0": "504b 00708" is 10 chars, should be "504b 0708", 9 chars, for the PK\x07\x08 split/spanned-archive signature). Worse than a simple misspelling: `_view_starts_with_zip_signature` always compares a substring sized to `len(_ZIP_SIGNATURES[0])` (9 chars) against the tuple, so the 10-char third entry can NEVER match even if correctly spelled -- it's dead code.
- Verified by simulating the exact comparison logic with a correctly-spelled 9-char PK 07 08 signature string -- confirmed `in SIGS` returns False.
- Filed: https://github.com/mawelborn/ZipContents/issues/5

## #631 Paste Plus (ggets/Sublime_PastePlus)
- Last modified: 2021-12-27. Not archived. No issues.
- Read source (pasteplus.py): Windows-only clipboard-paste enhancer handling file-drop (CF_HDROP) clipboard content via pywin32.
- Investigated two hypotheses from source review, both ruled out by live testing:
  1. `OpenClipboard()`/`CloseClipboard()` asymmetry: CloseClipboard is only called inside the `if IsClipboardFormatAvailable` branch, suggesting a leaked system-wide clipboard lock when the clipboard has neither text nor CF_HDROP data. Reproduced the exact WinAPI call sequence via ctypes (pywin32 dependency install got orphan-pruned on restart, same rig gotcha as #620 UrlConverter) -- `GetOpenClipboardWindow()` confirmed the clipboard was NOT left locked; Windows released it once the calling context returned, contrary to the naive reading of the code.
  2. Multi-selection replace loop (`for s in soa: self.view.replace(edit, s, data)`) looked like a classic stale-offset corruption bug when selections have mismatched lengths. Reproduced live with a temporary TextCommand and two differently-positioned selections -- result was correct ("XXXXXXXXXX XXXXXXXXXX CCCC"), because `view.sel()` returns a live Selection object whose regions are auto-adjusted by Sublime after each edit within the same edit transaction.
- Conclusion: no confirmed defect, not filed. Test remnants removed.

## #636 Coreboot syntax (coreboot/sublime-text-coreboot-syntax)
- Repo is a read-only GitHub mirror of `review.coreboot.org`'s Gerrit repo; GitHub issues are disabled entirely -- no reachable venue to file into, regardless of outcome.
- Installed cleanly via real Package Control API (`install_package`, non-dependency package, survived registration), console clean.
- Ran both bundled syntax tests live: pulled `syntax_test.asl` and `syntax_test.cb` from the repo, opened each with its auto-detected syntax, and verified every `^`/`<-` scope assertion against `view.scope_name()` (couldn't get ST's built-in `run_syntax_tests`/`build syntax_test` runner to produce visible output in the portable -- no output panel or console line appeared despite the command completing without error; fell back to a manual assertion-parser reimplementing the caret/arrow column convention, re-derived and cross-checked empirically against known-good lines before trusting it).
- `syntax_test.asl` (ASL grammar): 226/226 assertions passed clean.
- `syntax_test.cb` (devicetree grammar): 3 of 61 assertions failed, all in the same spot -- **real, confirmed bug**. `coreboot-devicetree.sublime-syntax` line 211 embeds C highlighting inside register-value strings via `embed: scope:source.c#statements`, but the embedded region never actually tokenizes as C: every character in e.g. `register "simple_register" = "1"`'s value gets one flat `source.c.embedded.cb` scope with no `source.c` base scope and none of the C grammar's own scopes (`variable.other.indexed.c`, numeric-literal scopes, etc.) -- consistent with ST silently no-op'ing an embed whose referenced context (`source.c#statements`) doesn't resolve in the currently bundled C syntax, degrading to plain text. Verified live by scanning every column of the affected line and confirming the flat scope across the whole embedded span, not just an assertion-column mismatch.
- Conclusion: real defect found and verified, but not filed -- no issue tracker reachable (mirror, issues disabled; upstream lives in Gerrit, out of scope for this campaign's GitHub-issue-only filing process).

## #637 QuickTemplate (Go) (SharanSharathi/sublime_qtpl)
- Last pushed 2021-12-27, not archived, no existing issues (has_issues true, list empty).
- Ships a `.sublime-build` with a real compile-check build system (`qtc -file ... ; go build ... ; del ... ; echo completed!`), no bundled syntax test.
- Installed `qtc` (free `go install github.com/valyala/quicktemplate/qtc@latest`) per the never-skip-for-free-prereqs rule, then built a real minimal Go module (`go.mod`, `main.go`, `hello.qtpl`) with `quicktemplate` as a dependency.
- Syntax auto-detected correctly on `.qtpl` open. Ran the "Compile File" build variant live.
- **Real bug found and filed: SharanSharathi/sublime_qtpl#1.** The Windows `shell_cmd` overrides chain commands with `;` (`qtc -file $file_name ; go build ... ; del ... ; echo completed!`), but `cmd.exe` (what ST's `shell_cmd` runs through on Windows) does not treat `;` as a command separator -- it's passed through as literal text, becoming trailing positional arguments to `qtc`, which Go's `flag` package silently ignores since `qtc` never reads `flag.Args()`. Confirmed live: the output panel only ever showed the `qtc` compile line, no `go build` output, no "completed!", `build_qtpl_binary.exe` was never created, and no `go.exe` process ever spawned -- all three Windows build variants ("Compile File", "Compile Dir", "Compile Dir without Line comments") have the identical bug. Net effect: on Windows the build system never actually verifies the generated Go code compiles, silently reporting success regardless of real template/Go errors.
- Console clean throughout (aside from the expected build behavior above).

## #641 LinkedData (blake-regalia/linked-data.syntaxes)
- Actively maintained (pushed 2022-12-08), 31 issues total, extensive existing tracker covering SPARQL/Turtle scoping edge cases (property paths, GROUP BY, DESCRIBE, case-sensitivity, triple-quote strings, etc.) -- most common defect classes already tracked. 2 currently-open bugs (nested blank node property paths; `$` context evaluation, wontfix) left alone since already known.
- **Methodology note, not a filed bug:** this package's `.sublime-syntax` files are unusually large (`trig.sublime-syntax` 3.33MB, `turtle.sublime-syntax` 3.28MB, `shex.sublime-syntax` 1.73MB, `sparql.sublime-syntax` 1.80MB -- normal syntax files are tens of KB). Immediately after a fresh Package Control install (and again after a full portable restart before a `pip`-style Package Control re-scan completed), `sublime.load_resource()`/`sublime.list_syntaxes()` found **zero** resources from this package, not even the 727-byte LICENSE file -- looked like a total package-load failure with no console error. Waiting ~15-20s longer resolved it: ST's resource indexer just needs much longer than usual to scan these oversized files. Confirmed not a real defect (fully reproducible timing artifact, not filed) -- but noting the methodology fix for future large-syntax-file packages in this campaign: always allow extra settle time before concluding "package failed to load" when file sizes are this far outside the norm.
- Live-tested ShExC (`.shex`, shape with cardinality/facet constraints) and N-Quads (`.nq`, language-tagged literal, typed literal, named graph) once properly indexed: both auto-detected correctly, console clean, and `view.scope_name()` spot checks confirmed accurate contextual subject/predicate/object/graph role-tracking (`meta.term.role.*`), correct language-tag and datatype-separator scoping -- non-trivial grammar behaving correctly.
- Conclusion: no new defect found this pass, not filed.

## #642 Expand and Edit (aafulei/sublime-expand-and-edit)
- Not archived, last pushed 2021-11-16. No existing issues. No default key bindings shipped (all commented out in the keymap files per package rules); commands reachable via Command Palette.
- Read `expand_and_edit.py`: `ExpandSwapCommand` implements a two-step "mark region, then swap with a second region" feature using a module-level `g_swap_center` dict keyed by view id, reset on any buffer edit (`on_modified_async`) or most other commands (`ExpandSwapListener.on_post_text_command`, which resets on anything NOT in `{"drag_select", "move", "move_to", "expand_swap_word", "expand_swap_subword"}`).
- **Suspected but NOT confirmed:** the exclusion list names the outer aliases `expand_swap_word`/`expand_swap_subword` (what the Command Palette/keymap actually invoke), but those aliases internally call `self.view.run_command("expand_swap")` -- a second, separate command whose name (`expand_swap`, no suffix) is NOT in the exclusion list. If nested `run_command` calls fire their own `on_post_text_command` event (normal Sublime behavior for real keypress/palette-triggered invocations), the listener would immediately reset the swap state right after step 1 sets it up, silently breaking the whole two-step swap feature on every real use.
- **Could not confirm live this session:** testing requires genuine keypress/command-palette dispatch for `ViewEventListener.on_post_text_command` to fire at all -- confirmed via a monkey-patched diagnostic that calling `view.run_command('expand_swap_word')` from eval_python never fires the listener (consistent with the known eval_python-dispatch-bypass limitation, see [[feedback_on_text_command_hooks_dont_fire_via_eval_python]]), so this harness can't distinguish "works correctly" from "the bug exists but my test can't see it." `computer-use` was unavailable this session (false-Escape-stop glitch, see [[computer_use_false_escape_stop]]), which is the only reliable way to get real event dispatch. Verified the swap's core replace-logic is sound when state does persist (via direct eval_python, bypassing the listener question entirely): two `expand_swap_word` calls on "alpha" and "gamma" in "alpha beta gamma delta" correctly produced "gamma beta alpha delta", status cleared correctly. Console clean throughout.
- **RESOLVED, hypothesis REFUTED (retested same session after `computer-use`'s false-Escape-stop glitch was cleared -- root cause was an unrelated stuck M365Copilot.exe process/launcher, killed and reconnected).** Drove the real Command Palette via genuine keypress dispatch (`Ctrl+Shift+P`, typed "Expand Swap Word" character-by-character via `press_key` -- bulk `type_text` unreliably tripled input on this window, a tool quirk not a package bug -- then Down+Return to disambiguate from "Expand Swap Subword"). A monkey-patched diagnostic on `ExpandSwapListener.on_post_text_command` confirmed real events fire for genuine dispatch (unlike eval_python-issued commands, which never trigger it at all -- see [[feedback_on_text_command_hooks_dont_fire_via_eval_python]]), but the only commands logged were `move_to`/`move` (palette list-navigation artifacts) -- **neither `expand_swap_word` nor the inner `expand_swap` ever appeared in the log**, meaning nested `self.view.run_command()` calls issued from within a command's own `run()` do NOT refire `ViewEventListener.on_post_text_command` for the nested call. The suspected self-cancel bug can't happen because the premise (nested calls refire the event) was wrong. Full live swap on "alpha"/"gamma" in "alpha beta gamma delta" completed correctly end-to-end via real Command Palette invocations: status set correctly after step 1 (survived intact, still showing `Swapping "alpha" @ Line 1` right before step 2), buffer correctly became "gamma beta alpha delta" after step 2, status cleared correctly. Console clean throughout.
- Conclusion: no defect, not filed. Good instance of campaign discipline paying off -- the pre-live-test suspicion was reasonable from reading the source alone, but wrong.

## #643 Fold Javascript Functions (LuckyKat/sublime-fold-functions)
- Not archived, last pushed 2021-11-09. 6 issues, all closed (ST3/ST4 compat questions resolved, constructor-folding, ES6 support already addressed).
- Read `foldfunctions.py`: `CursorListener.on_selection_modified_async` is a global `EventListener` (fires for every view's selection changes, not just JS files) doing `syntax = view.settings().get('syntax'); ... "JavaScript" in syntax` -- widget views (console panel, Goto Line/Find inputs, quick-panel filters) commonly have `syntax` unset (`None`), which would `TypeError`. The package's own shipped default settings set `select_to_unfold: true`, so Python's `or` short-circuit does NOT save the crash-with-defaults case (confirmed by reading `foldfunctions.sublime-settings` before assuming a possible mitigating default).
- **Methodology note along the way:** first live-install attempt showed the package's own module never appearing in `sys.modules` and no "reloading plugin" console line at all (Package Control reported success, no errors) -- looked like a serious package-load failure. Manual `importlib.import_module` proved the file itself has no syntax/import errors. Restarted the portable to test cold-start load: it DID load correctly that time (`reloading plugin Fold Javascript Functions.foldfunctions` appeared), then got removed again by Package Control's orphan-scan (the already-documented `installed_packages`-persistence gotcha, see baton). Reinstalled once more without restarting: loaded correctly immediately, "reloading plugin" line present right away. Concluded the original no-load was a one-off transient glitch in this test session, not a reproducible package defect -- don't over-conclude "package failed to load" from a single miss; retry once before writing it up as a finding.
- **Real bug found, reproduced live, and filed: LuckyKat/sublime-fold-functions#8.** Opened the console panel (`window.get_output_panel('console')`, confirmed `syntax` setting is `None`), moved the selection within it (first via raw `view.sel()`/`run_command('move')` API pokes -- no crash, but that was BEFORE discovering the plugin module wasn't loaded yet in that attempt, a red herring, not evidence of anything). After confirming the module was genuinely loaded (`sys.modules` contained it, "reloading plugin" line present) and retrying the identical selection-change test, got a clean console traceback: `TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not a container or iterable` at exactly `foldfunctions.py` line 34, matching the hypothesis exactly. This crashes on ordinary console use (which most developers open regularly), not an edge case, and happens with the package's own out-of-the-box default settings.

## #644 42 Headers (Globidev/Sublime-Text-42-Headers)
- Not archived, last pushed 2022-02-07, niche package for 42-school students. 7 issues, all closed.
- **False alarm avoided by live-testing before filing:** `generate_header()` calls `settings.timestamp(time)`, passing the raw `time` *module* (not a datetime) into a function that calls `stamp.strftime(...)`. Looked like a guaranteed `AttributeError` crash on every single header generation (the plugin's entire core purpose) from static reading alone. Tested live -- it works fine: `stamp.strftime(fmt)` where `stamp` is the `time` module resolves to `time.strftime(fmt)`, a real module-level function using `time.localtime()` by default -- clever/confusing but valid Python, not a bug. Would have been a wasted or wrong filing.
- **Real bug found, reproduced live, and filed: Globidev/Sublime-Text-42-Headers#24 -- DATA LOSS, high severity.** `toggle_headerCommand.disable()` recomputes a *fresh* header (current username/filename/timestamp) and erases `Region(0, len(header))` from the buffer, instead of measuring the header actually present. The header template (`headers/c_family.py`) uses minimum-width `%-51s`/`%-43s`/etc. format specs (pad-if-shorter, NOT truncate-if-longer). Reproduced live: inserted a header on a 4-line `test.c` (buffer 928 chars), changed the `login` setting to a longer value (an entirely ordinary settings change, no file rename needed), ran `toggle_header` again to remove it -- **the entire file's contents were silently erased**, not just the header (confirmed root cause directly: regenerated header came out to 929 chars against a 928-char buffer, so `Region(0, 929)` clamped to erase everything). No error, no warning, no confirmation prompt. Any user who changes their configured username, or whose filename is long enough, can lose a whole file's contents on next header-toggle.

## #645 BBC BASIC Syntax (gerph/sublimetext-bbcbasic-syntax)
- Not archived, last pushed 2021-11-08, small (138-line) hand-written `.sublime-syntax`, no bundled test. 6 issues, all closed.

Checked closed issue #3 ("ORIGIN highlights the OR only") -- the landed fix just added `ORIGIN` as its own explicit alternative in the giant keyword list rather than fixing the root cause (no boundary), so the identical class of bug still applies to every OTHER keyword substring, and to any identifier not specifically whitelisted the way `ORIGIN` now is.
- **Real bug found, reproduced live, and filed: gerph/sublimetext-bbcbasic-syntax#7.** Installed live, opened a real `.bbc` file with `10 TOTAL% = 100` / `20 ORB = 5`, checked `view.scope_name()` per character: `TOTAL%`'s leading `TO` gets `keyword.control.bbcbasic` while the rest (`TAL%`) gets `variable.integer.bbcbasic` -- the variable name visibly splits into two colors; `ORB`'s leading `OR` gets `keyword.control.bbcbasic` while `B` gets `variable.float.bbcbasic` -- literally the same keyword (`OR`) from the closed issue #3, just on an identifier that wasn't specifically whitelisted like `ORIGIN` was. Affects any variable/procedure name starting with one of the many short keywords in the big alternation (`TO`, `OR`, `ON`, `IF`, `FOR`, `LEN`, `INT`, `LOG`, etc.) -- a common naming collision risk in a language with lots of short reserved words. Console clean throughout.

## #647 Simple Ifdef (rumly111/simpleifdef)
- Not archived, last pushed 2021-11-05, ST3-era plugin (per its own description). 3 issues, all closed.
- Initial hypothesis from reading `simpleifdef.py`: `IfdefHighlighter` stores `self._groups`/`self._regions` as instance state on a SINGLE global `EventListener` shared across all views, fully cleared and rebuilt on every `_rescan(view)` call -- not scoped per-view. A background view getting rescanned (e.g. `on_modified` firing for a non-active view) while a different view is active would corrupt `on_selection_modified`'s data for the active view. Set up a live two-file (`a.cpp`/`b.cpp`) repro to test this directly.
- **Found something more fundamental first, which made the shared-state test moot:** `_rescan()`'s `view.find_by_selector("meta.preprocessor keyword.control.import")` returned `[]` for BOTH files. Checked the actual scope Sublime's current bundled `Packages/C++/C++.sublime-syntax` assigns to `#ifdef`/`#endif`: `keyword.control.directive.conditional.if.c++` / `...endif.c++` under `meta.preprocessor.c++` -- the `keyword.control.import` half of the selector never matches current scope names (`keyword.control.directive.conditional.*`, not `keyword.control.import.*`). The plugin's core feature -- the only thing it does -- silently never fires on any current Sublime Text install, for any file. The shared-state design issue I set out to test is real but moot in practice while this is broken, since there's nothing to corrupt.
- **Real bug found, reproduced live, and filed: rumly111/simpleifdef#4.** Console clean throughout (no errors -- it just silently no-ops, which is why nobody would notice from a crash/traceback).

## #649 Strings Resource File (p4t5h3/strings-resource-file-language-for-sublime-text)
- **Archived** (last pushed 2022-01-11). Well-tested for its era -- has a bundled `tests/syntax_test_main.strings` (327 assertions) and closed issue #3 set up CI to run it. 5 issues, all closed.
- ST's built-in `run_syntax_tests`/`build syntax_test` runner again produced no visible output in the portable (same limitation as Coreboot syntax, #636) -- fell back to the same manual `^`/`<-` assertion-parser used there (adapted for this file's `/* ... */`-wrapped comment-assertion style instead of `//`/`#`).
- 52 of 327 assertions failed, ALL on the same thing: every format-placeholder (`%@`, `%d`, `%D`, `%u`, `%x`, etc.) inside a quoted string only gets plain `string.quoted.double.strings`, never the expected `constant.other.placeholder.strings` layered on top. Verified directly against the live view (not just the test script) to rule out a column-math bug: confirmed `%`/`d` in `"a %d"` really do get flat `string.quoted.double.strings` only.
- Root cause found in the repo's own history, not filed as new: closed issue #4 ("Detect formatting placeholders in strings") WAS actually implemented -- commit `40f20875` ("Closes #4: Highlighting formatting placeholders") is real and present on the default branch, and the syntax file (fetched from current HEAD) does contain the correct `constant.other.placeholder.strings` match rule in the right place (first rule in the `string` context, before the closing-quote rule). But the Package Control release tag actually installed (`1.1.0`, commit `57917897`) **predates** that fix commit -- no release was ever cut after it. So the fix genuinely exists in source but was never shipped, and since the repo is now archived, never will be.
- Not filed (repo archived -- filing "please cut a release" on an archived repo goes nowhere) and not otherwise actionable; documented here since it's a real, precisely-diagnosed gap between the source and what users actually get via Package Control, distinct from a code bug.

## #650 0x0 (axsuul/sublime-0x0)
- Not archived, last pushed 2022-02-04, no existing issues (this would be the first).
- Read `sublime-0x0.py`: `Post0x0Command.run()` (a `TextCommand`, runs on the main thread) does the upload synchronously -- `urllib2.urlopen(request).read()` with no `timeout=` argument and no background thread/`set_timeout_async`.
- **Real bug found, reproduced live, and filed: axsuul/sublime-0x0#1 (the repo's first issue).** Monkeypatched `urllib2.urlopen` in the loaded module to `time.sleep(4)` before returning a canned response, then timed `view.run_command('post0x0')` directly: blocked for exactly `4.0015s`, matching the simulated delay precisely -- confirms the command has no async dispatch at all. Independently corroborated by sublime-mcp's own dispatch monitor, which separately logged `[sublime-mcp] slow dispatch ... took 4.00s` for the same call. Since there's no timeout on the real network call either, a slow/unresponsive `0x0.st` or an ordinary network hiccup freezes the entire Sublime Text UI (every view, every pane) for an unbounded duration in real use.

## #651 SendCode (randy3k/SendCode)
- Not archived, actively used, last pushed 2022-11-04. 17+ open issues already, spanning macOS/Linux/Windows terminal integrations (Terminus, ConEmu/Cmder, iTerm, tmux, RStudio, etc.) -- most known-broken integrations already tracked. Scoped this pass to the Windows-only code paths this rig can actually test live rather than macOS/Linux (untestable here) or deep GUI-app integrations (would need RStudio/ConEmu/Cmder actually installed).
- Read `code_sender/conemu/__init__.py`'s `_send_to_conemu()`: builds the ConEmuC.exe command line via plain Python string formatting (`'{} -GuiMacro:0 Paste(2,"{}")'.format(conemuc, escape_dquote(cmd))`) and passes the whole thing as a single **string** to `subprocess.check_call()` -- `conemuc` (the path to ConEmuC.exe, real default installs like Cmder's are under `C:\Program Files\cmder\...`) is never quoted or passed as a list element.
- **Real bug found, reproduced live, and filed: randy3k/SendCode#176 -- CWE-428 unquoted search path.** Constructed the exact SendCode command-line pattern with a fake `conemuc` path containing a space, placed a decoy executable (`whoami.exe`, copied) at the WRONG Windows break-point path (the classic unquoted-path parsing gotcha: CreateProcess tries progressively longer space-delimited prefixes as candidate executables when given an unquoted string), and nothing at the real/correct path. Ran the SendCode-style string via `subprocess.run()`: `returncode 1, stdout b'', stderr b' '`. Then ran the decoy directly with the same trailing args for comparison: **byte-for-byte identical output** -- conclusively proving Windows launched the decoy at the wrong breakpoint instead of the real target. In a real install, any executable existing at a space-delimited prefix of the user's actual ConEmuC.exe path causes SendCode to silently run that program (with the user's code/text as its arguments) instead of sending to the terminal, no error shown. Cleaned up decoy test files after confirming.

## #654 GotoEndOfLineOrScope (SublimeText/GoToEndOfLineOrScope)
- Not archived, last pushed 2021-10-15. 1 open (enhancement), 1 closed bug (comment-at-line-start edge case, already fixed).
- **Suspected bug from static reading, disproven live (2 separate constructed scenarios):** `calculate_eol_positions()`'s fallback branch (`if not desired_end_pos: if len(eol_positions) > 1: desired_end_pos = before_scope_pos`) references `before_scope_pos`, which is only assigned inside `if relevant_token:` -- looked like a guaranteed `UnboundLocalError` whenever no scope match exists on the line AND `eol_positions` has 2 distinct values (soft vs hard EOL).
  1. First tried trailing-whitespace-on-a-line as the source of soft/hard EOL divergence -- wrong mental model; `get_logical_eol_positions` computes EOL from visual *word-wrap* layout (`text_to_layout`/`layout_to_text`), not trailing whitespace. No crash (confirmed via console, not just the Python call's return).
  2. Corrected the setup: created a genuinely word-wrapped line (`word_wrap: true`, narrow `wrap_width`, confirmed via `view.text_to_layout` that the line's start and end land on different visual rows) with no comment content, cursor at the hard EOL. Still no crash.
  3. Re-derived the logic by hand to understand why: whenever `desired_end_pos` ends up `None` (the precondition for reaching the buggy branch), the cursor must already be at the line's hard EOL -- and at that exact position, the "soft EOL" (end of the cursor's *own* visual row, which for the last row equals the hard EOL) trivially collapses `eol_positions` to a single value, never `>1`. The crash precondition appears to be a logically unreachable combination, not just hard to hit in practice.
- Smoke-tested the actual documented feature instead: two-press behavior on `x = 1  # a comment` (default `eol_first`) -- first press correctly landed on end-of-line (pos 18), second press correctly jumped back to just before the comment (pos 7), matching the README's described UX exactly.
- Conclusion: no defect found; the static-analysis suspicion was reasonable but wrong. Not filed. Good instance of campaign discipline (verify live, including checking console for swallowed exceptions per the Paste As Column precedent) catching a false positive before filing.

## #657 StandardFormat (bcomnes/sublime-standard-format)
- Not archived, actively maintained (pushed 2025-11-21), 29 issues total. 2 open bugs already tracked: #91 `KeyError: 'jsx'` (reported 2023, maintainer acked "I'll take a look" but never landed a fix) and #80 (eslint_d leaks errors). Reviewed #91 for root cause and precise confirmation rather than duplicate-filing.
- Root cause traced statically: `run()` does an unguarded `selectors[view_syntax]` dict lookup (line 347) when `view_syntax` is in the `extensions` allow-list. Checked the *default* `StandardFormat.sublime-settings`: default `extensions` is `["js", "jsx"]`, but default `selectors` only has `html`/`vue` keys -- no `jsx` -- meaning this crashes out-of-the-box, not from user misconfiguration (the original reporter's traceback was widely assumed to be their own custom settings).
- **Confirmed live via real reproduction, added precise root-cause diagnosis as a comment on the existing open issue rather than filing a duplicate: bcomnes/sublime-standard-format#91 (comment).** The crash requires `get_command()` to find a real formatter binary in PATH first (`standard`/`semistandard`/`ts-standard`, none installed on this rig) -- rather than install a heavyweight npm toolchain just for this, monkeypatched `get_command` to return a real resolvable binary (`['node', '--version']`) so execution reaches the actual crash site without needing the full external tool. First attempt used a fake `['echo']` stub, which tripped a *different* crash first (Windows: `shutil.which('echo', ...)` returns `None` since `echo` is a shell builtin not a real .exe, so `command[0]` became `None` and crashed in `replace_placeholders` instead) -- switched to a real resolvable binary and got the intended `KeyError: 'jsx'` at exactly line 347, confirming the diagnosis cleanly on a completely default-settings `.jsx` file.

## #658 MayaSublime (justinfx/MayaSublime)
- Not archived, 30 issues (most closed, actively triaged historically). Core feature (send code to a running Autodesk Maya via commandPort) needs a real, non-free, heavyweight Maya install to test end-to-end -- out of scope for this rig. Found a much more fundamental, Maya-independent bug instead: the plugin fails to *load at all*.
- `MayaSublime.py` line 13: `from telnetlib import Telnet` -- `telnetlib` was deprecated in Python 3.11 and removed in Python 3.13. No `.python-version` file ships with the package to pin it to an older host.
- **Real bug found, reproduced live, and filed: justinfx/MayaSublime#44.** Fresh install on Sublime Text 4215 (which offers a newer python3.14 plugin host for unpinned packages) crashed immediately on first load, before any Maya connection is ever attempted: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'telnetlib'`. The entire plugin -- every command -- is non-functional.
- **Honest scope caveat, checked before overclaiming a fix:** tried the standard `.python-version: 3.8` fix (per [[feedback_python_version_retest]]) by extracting the package to a loose directory with the pin added -- it STILL failed identically. Root cause: this specific portable test rig only has the python3.14 and python3.3 hosts available (per the baton's own "Test rig" notes), not python3.8, so the pin fix genuinely couldn't be verified here. Reported this honestly in the filed issue rather than falsely claiming the fix was confirmed -- noted that most current real-world ST4 installs likely still default to the 3.8 host (which still has telnetlib) and may not be hit by this yet, but any build offering a newer default host will be, and everyone will be eventually as ST phases out older hosts. Cleaned up the test extraction directory after confirming.

## #662 Status Bar JsonPath (akirk/StatusBarJsonPath)
- Not archived (pushed 2023-07), 2 issues before mine (#6 feature request, #1 install, closed). Package Control name has spaces: "Status Bar JsonPath" (`StatusBarJsonPath` = "not available").
- Real bug FILED as akirk/StatusBarJsonPath#8: `find_end_quote` starts `bt = i` (the quote itself), so the backslash-counting loop never runs and every `\"` ends the string. Any JSON with an escaped quote before the cursor gives a wrong path. Confirmed offline with the module's own function, then live in the portable (installed 1.0.0, same code): `{"a": "x\"y", "b": {"c": 1}}` with cursor on the `1` gives `a`, expected `b.c`; control without the escape gives `b.c`. Also verified the suggested fix (`bt = i - 1`, break on `(i - bt) % 2 == 1`) on 4 cases. Posted body re-read: backslash lines intact.
- Also noticed (not filed, separate/minor): `get_json_path` abort paths return `(None, None)` and callers do `len()`/`join` on it; `key = frame['key'].replace(...)` result is unused. Not reachable without a race or unusual keys, so left out per one-issue-per-finding and user-reachable rules.

## #663 Firebase Rules Syntax (jingyuexing/Sublime-Firebase-Syntax)
- Not archived (last push 2021-09), zero issues. Syntax-only package (Firebase.sublime-syntax, scope source.firerules), no bundled syntax tests. PC name "Firebase Rules Syntax" 0.0.1; syntax registered ~10s after install.
- Real bug FILED as Sublime-Firebase-Syntax#1: a negated call `!get(...)` / `!exists(...)` loses function highlighting because the `function` rule needs `[.\s(]` before the name. For `get`, the unbounded `access-control` rule (`\b{{access_control}}`, no trailing boundary) then scopes it `storage.modifier` and pushes an unnamed context that only pops on `,:;`, so the rest of the statement is unscoped. Confirmed live with view.scope_name() per token, with a control (`if get(` is correct: support.function, variables and `false` scoped). `!exists(` just leaves `exists` unscoped.
- Other observations NOT filed (minor/cosmetic, one-issue-per-finding): `==`/`||` get the assignment scope, `&&` is matched as two `&` (the `&&` rule is unreachable), `in|function|true|...` constants have no word boundaries, `number-binary` `([01])+` shadows numbers. ## #675 BinViewer (AetelFinch/BinViewer)
- Repo is ARCHIVED (last push 2022-08-08), no issues. Single command `bin_viewer` (81 lines) showing a popup with the binary form of selected decimal/hex numbers. Not installed (archived-repo policy); the pure conversion function was tested directly by importing the module with stubbed `sublime`/`sublime_plugin`.
- REAL BUG, NOT FILED (archived, no venue): `convertToBin` sizes the field from `abs(n).bit_length()` (8/16/32...), then masks negatives to that width, so negatives whose magnitude fills the width wrap to a wrong, positive-looking value: -129 -> `01111111` (should be 16-bit `1111111101111111`), -200 -> `00111000`, -255 -> `00000001`, -32769 -> `0111111111111111`, -65535 -> `0000000000000001`. -1, -128, -256, -32768 come out right. Confirmed with the module's own function (`%TEMP%\bv_check.py`).
- Add to the "archived-repo findings, review with Donald" list (CP Parser, Search in Project, Emoji Code, StringsResourceFile, BinViewer).
- Conclusion: skipped (archived), not filed.

## #705 addendum (2026-09-29) Buildview follow-up -- piping study + issue
- Studied Buildview's view-to-view piping (see GhostShell/ai/BUILDVIEW_STUDY.md, commit 4b7f839): 9 live scenarios + benchmark on `PipeViews`.
- Real-flow check of one suspicion: after a key-binding build, a build started WITHOUT the key context (menu / command palette / other package) leaves the Build output tab corrupted (`exec` panel `B\n[Finished in 47ms]` vs tab `fi[Finished in 47ms]`); recovers on the next key-binding build. Cause: `prepare_copy` (reset read-head + clear dest) only runs from `on_query_context` for `build_fake`; `on_modified` keeps piping from the stale read-head. (My first attempt was contaminated by calling `get_output_panel("exec")`, which CLEARS the panel and triggers the pipe -- use `find_output_panel` to read.)
- FILED: rctay/sublime-text-buildview#39 (with two hardening suggestions: reset when source is shorter than the read-head; check dest.size() == read-head and rebuild from source).
- Earlier: commented cause/workaround on #32 and #38 (defaults invisible until restart; `set_scratch(None)` TypeError).
- Cleanup: package removed, in-memory prefs not saved, views closed.

## SublimeLinter-phplint (queue v2 #10, 3.2.0)
- Installed live (wrapper loads clean). It wraps icosaedro PHPLint (`phpl`), a PHP 5/7-era tool. Downloaded PHPLint 4.2.0 (2020) and ran it on PHP 8.4.25: it cannot run at all. Layer 1: `stdlib/autoload.php` gives up on registering its autoloader because `is_array(spl_autoload_functions())` is always true on PHP 8 (it returned false when empty on PHP 7) -> `Class ... ResourceOutputStream not found`. Layer 2 (after patching that in a scratch copy): its own error handler turns E_DEPRECATED into an exception, and `UString implements Serializable` is deprecated in 8.x -> fatal.
- The linter is effectively dead on any current PHP; open upstream issue #40 already says it is disabled for deprecated PHP. **Nothing filed** (no new information; not a bug in the wrapper).

## SublimeLinter-erlc (2026-10-01)
- Erlang/OTP 29 (erts 17.1, C:\Users\donal\tools\erlang) already installed. Live: erlc prints diagnostics on STDERR (stdout empty); wrapper has error_stream = STREAM_STDOUT, so SL starts erlc with stderr=None (inherits Sublime's invalid GUI stderr). Result: NO results ever, and erlc/the VM crashes whenever it has a diagnostic to print ("Runtime terminating during boot ({badarg,[{io,put_chars,[standard_error,...") leaving a ~2 MB erl_crash.dump in the source folder on every lint. Not reproducible from a shell/pythonw with explicit pipes; found by reading SL's Popen (stderr only piped when the linter asks for it). Verified fix: error_stream = STREAM_STDERR (set on the live class): correct lines/columns (also after non-ASCII text; erlc counts characters), no crash dump. STREAM_BOTH removes the crash but SL only logs stderr as a warning and parses nothing. `-o .` leaving .beam next to the source is DOCUMENTED (README option `o`), not filed. Filed SublimeLinter/SublimeLinter-erlc#9 (tracker had nothing relevant).
- Tooling note: to test a changed SL wrapper class quickly, set the class attribute on the running class (Linter.__subclasses__() filtered by .name); reloading from an unpacked Packages copy does not reliably replace a class loaded from the .sublime-package.
- Cleanup: wrapper + unpacked copy removed, linters/debug settings cleared, crash dumps/beams deleted, no dialogs.

## PHPUnitKit (2026-10-01)
- gerardroche/sublime-phpunit (PHPUnitKit 3.19.4; .no-sublime-package, unpacked into Packages). PHPUnit 12.5 phar + a Composer-style vendor\bin\phpunit.bat launcher in %TEMP%/puk_proj (winget PHP has no php.ini, so the launcher passes -d extension_dir/-d extension=mbstring). Live on a restarted portable: "PHPUnit: Test File" shows the full run in the exec panel (text-ui-result syntax), the failing test with accented text is shown correctly; "Test Nearest" runs only the test under the cursor (1 test). Nothing filed.
- IMPORTANT RIG LESSON: a package's own Packages/<pkg>/Preferences.sublime-settings (how PHPUnitKit and others ship their defaults, e.g. "phpunit.composer": true) is merged into the global preferences ONLY AT SUBLIME STARTUP, not when the package is installed or when preferences are touched. My first run right after install gave `PHPUnit: 'phpunit not found'` because every `phpunit.*` setting read None; after a restart it worked. Verified with a throwaway package (ZZPrefTest): None before restart, 123 after. So for any package that ships package-level Preferences defaults, restart the portable before judging it (earlier conclusions about such packages made without a restart could be wrong).
- Cleanup: package, project data, test package removed.

## CodeTime (swdc-sublime) (2026-10-01): NOT INSTALLED/RUN (outward-facing); static review only; issue swdc-sublime#57
Not run: on load it registers an anonymous account with software.com and sends activity (OS username, hostname, timezone, global git email, file names, project path/name, keystrokes, repo remote url). Donald: no install; he calls it malware - I disagreed with the label (README discloses tracking; telemetry opt-out setting software_telemetry_on exists; selling unproven, policy page on moved domain unreadable) but agreed it is a serious privacy concern. Verified statically: raw `git config remote.origin.url` is sent as repo_identifier (credentials in URL would leak) -> filed #57 (facts only, no malware claim). Domain facts: bare software.com fails TLS (handshake failure, Donald saw ERR_SSL_VERSION_OR_CIPHER_MISMATCH); www/api/app.software.com have valid certs but GET / 301s to antenna.dev; BUT a POST to api.software.com/data/ping returned 403 (CloudFront), not a redirect, so I did NOT file a 'plugin broken by redirect' issue (unproven). Package Control channel report not made: channel maintainer ban. Repo dormant since 2024-04.

## CodeTime follow-up (2026-10-02): Devin's independent review + correction of #57
Donald asked me to launch Devin for an opinion. `devin -p` (print mode, permission auto) first run failed (web fetch needs confirmation in non-interactive mode; did NOT use --permission-mode dangerous). Second run on a local read-only copy of the source worked. Devin: do NOT recommend; confirmed raw remote URL w/o credential stripping, tracking on by default, README silent on opt-out and on selling/third parties; "malware" debatable, service state unknowable from code. Devin also pointed at lib/TrackerManager.py encrypt_and_save: plain-text values (file name/path, project name/dir, repo name/identifier/owner/branch/tag) are POSTed with their BLAKE2b hash to /api/v1/user/encrypted_data. I verified that (hash_value lines 195-215, encrypt_and_save 229-240) and CORRECTED my issue #57 (events carry only hashes; plaintext goes in that separate POST) and its title. Lesson: my first #57 text had the data path partly wrong; verify the whole path before filing.

## SublimeLinter-erblint (2026-10-02): defect verified, NOT filed (repo has issues + discussions disabled)

## ghc PR #10: kaste's review questions (2026-10-02 21:34-21:39), answered
(1) "Examples? Naively one tab counts 8": real GHC 9.14.1 JSON columns: `f = 1 +<TAB>undefinedA` -> col 9 (tab=8 columns would give 16), `g =<TAB>undefinedB` -> col 9 (naive 12), `<TAB><TAB>undefinedC` -> col 17 (both agree). (2) "7e145114 removed tab_width in core; re-introduce? other linters?": that code mapped by subtracting (tab_width-1) per tab; run with 8 it returns index 7/3 (the tab) instead of 8/4, right only for leading tabs. Only ghc found. gcc 16.1: default -fdiagnostics-column-unit=display is tab-stop based with a file argument (col 44 vs byte 23 on a 3-tab line), BUT SublimeLinter-gcc (stdin, column_unit utf8) underlined the right token (start col 22) in SL, so no need. Recommended keeping convert_column local to ghc; offered to remove it. Posted + corrected one sentence (first version said the old code 'gives 16 and 12', which was the naive column, not what the code returns).

- IMESupport (2026-10-06): NOT tested live, and installing it was a mistake. On load the plugin calls globalhook.setup(), which loads imesupport_hook_x64.dll; the DLL calls SetWindowsHookEx(WH_GETMESSAGE, ..., hModule, 0), a system-wide hook (thread id 0), so Windows injects the DLL into other programs on the desktop. After the install the DLL was loaded in AppActions, sihost, svchost, SynTPEnh and unsecapp (real programs, not the test Sublime). I closed the test Sublime at once (that ends the hook) and did nothing else to those programs; the DLL stays loaded in them until they restart, so D:\st_portable_4200\Data\Packages\IMESupport could not be recycled yet (locked). Recycle it after a restart or sign-out. Design is from 2015 (inline IME composition), not filed. Lesson: before installing a package that ships .dll/.exe files or mentions Windows hooks, read its source first (show_pkg_code / unpacked folder), never run it on the live desktop.

- IMESupport follow-up (2026-10-06): reported to Package Control as sublimehq/package_control_channel#9600 (system-wide SetWindowsHookEx hook; DLL left loaded in five real programs). Donald told me to report it to Package Control, not to the author. Leftover folder D:\st_portable_4200\Data\Packages\IMESupport to be recycled after his next Windows restart.

- FileSystem Autocompletion (lingo/sublime-fscompletion, 4200, 2026-10-06; packed install, loads after a restart): file_system_comp_trigger (alt+ctrl+/) completes D:/st_portable_4200/Data/Pack -> Packages/ (Dir) with a popup. Paths with a drive letter other than the editor's current drive never complete: debug shows guessed_path C:/Users/donal/pro -> fuzzy_path /pro -> pattern /pro*. Cause (verified): fsutils.iglob wraps every letter, including the drive letter, in a [xX] class, and Python glob finds 0 matches for [cC]:/... but 8 for C:/Users/* (and 8 with only the rest classed). Paths with spaces (plain, quoted, or backslash-escaped) gave no popup in my tests (not investigated further). Commented the cause on the open, vague lingo/sublime-fscompletion#15 ('Simply doesn't work', same C:\da symptom) instead of filing a duplicate.

FOUND (two issues, filed): KristoforMaynard/SublimeChmod#2 (chmod() error handler uses e.message: on /etc/hostname 'Chmod a+x' gives AttributeError: 'PermissionError' object has no attribute 'message' instead of the dialog) and #3 (done() builds 'chmod <mode> <path>' and uses cmd.split(), so a path with a space makes the system chmod fail and the fallback only knows r/w/x: 'u+s' on the spaced path gives KeyError 's'). Not tested: the sidebar command, Windows dialogs. Package and /tmp test files removed.

## BuildSock (iccir/BuildSock 0.3.0, WSL Linux ST 4200)

## Batch of small plugins (2026-10-07, eased list, portable 4200 / 3.3 host unless noted): Copy Python Import, Ruby Block Converter, DeWatermark, ParentalControl, Jasmine Scaffold, Pastery
Installed from Package Control; the raw-API installs were not seen by the resource index until each package was unpacked into Data\Packages and reloaded (known trap).
- Copy Python Import (odiroot): saved files give correct "from pkg.mod import ..." statements (method, class, constant, function). On an UNSAVED Python buffer nothing happens and no message is shown (clipboard unchanged; cause by reading: os.path.split(None) in _get_module_path). Issues are disabled and the newest commits are from a noreply address, so NOT reported.
- Ruby Block Converter (irohiroki): brace -> do/end and back work, including a brace inside a string; only cosmetic (do/end -> brace gives "{|x| puts x }"). Nothing filed.
- DeWatermark (djrobby): removes zero-width characters and fixes smart quotes; but HOMOGLYPH_MAP is applied to every character, so real Russian text (e.g. "xopowo" style mixes) and Greek capitals are silently rewritten. Filed djrobby/DeWatermark#1.
- ParentalControl (ilyakam): add/remove parentheses correct (inner pair removed at the cursor). Nothing filed.
- Jasmine Scaffold (cdwmyk): output only looked wrong because my test used spaces while the tab setting said tabs; not a defect. Nothing filed.
- Pastery (apas): Package Control serves v1.1.2 from 2016 (python_version 3.3); master (2025: duration/title settings, .python-version) was never tagged. Served version works with its default api_key "foo". The master code prints the full request address including the API key, but that is NOT in the served release, so not reported. Filed apas/pastery#12 (no release since 2016).
Lesson: Package Control serves the latest TAG, which can differ from the repo HEAD that I read; verify findings on the installed copy.

## 2026-10-07 audit through sublime-mcp tools only (4200 portable, palette installs)
- LSP 2.14.0: installed through the palette picker. No dialogs. Its import blocked the main thread for over 5 s while it wrote bytecode, which made one run_command call time out with a message blaming a native dialog (no dialog existed).
- LSP-tombi 1.0.0 (release): after install and after a restart the plugin loads on Python 3.3 and fails with SyntaxError at plugin.py line 52 (uri: str); its commands do nothing. Cause: .gitattributes has .python-version export-ignore, so the install archive has no .python-version. Filed sublimelsp/LSP-tombi#2. Retest with an unpacked copy of master plus .python-version in Packages\LSP-tombi: the plugin loads on 3.8, status bar shows "LSP: tombi (installing...)" then "LSP: tombi (bundled)", so the server was downloaded and started. The only difference from the failing install is the missing .python-version file.
- LSP-zuban 1.0.2 (release, 4200 portable): installed through the palette picker, loads on the 3.8 host with libraries lsp_utils and sublime_lib, no errors. It is off by default ("enabled": false); after "LSP: Enable Language Server Globally" the status bar shows "LSP: zuban (installing...)", but after about 8 minutes there were still no diagnostics for a deliberate type error, "LSP-zuban: check Current File" showed nothing, and the console had no error. RESOLVED: after restarting Sublime the status bar shows "LSP: zuban" and the deliberate type error on line 5 gets a red error mark, so zuban works. So the server did not start in the session where the package was installed and enabled; it started only after a restart. No issue filed.
- LSP-oxfmt 1.0.1 (release, 4200 portable): installed through the palette picker, loads on 3.8, no errors. No server started in the install session (status bar empty, "Format Document" did nothing for about 4 minutes). Same pattern as LSP-tombi, LSP-zuban: a new LSP-* wrapper installed during a session did not start its server until Sublime was restarted. Probably LSP behaviour, not the packages; no issue filed.
- LSP-oxlint 1.0.1 (release, 4200 portable): installed through the palette picker; after a restart the status bar showed "oxlint (installing...)" then "oxlint (bundled)", and warning marks appeared on the unused variable and the `debugger` line of a test .js file. PASS.

(5) After "exit", run_command reports "main-thread timeout ... a native dialog" although no dialog exists.
- sublime-mcp weaknesses seen: get_console visible mode ignores tail and returns the whole console; there is no reliable "install finished" signal for a package's own server install (status text stays "installing..."); run_command returns ok even when the command does not exist; get_console auto/captured mode missed the SyntaxError and new console output (complete=false); visible mode needs the window in front and force_focus is the only way; get_output_panel "Console" dumps everything; str_replace_based_edit_tool view on a folder says "file not found"; timeout message blames a native dialog when the main thread is just busy; type_text and key chords do not dispatch to a never-focused window (single keys work after a title-bar click).

## sublime-mcp and workflow findings from this session (2026-10-08 and 2026-10-09)
- Console capture: get_console mode=visible clicks at a fixed spot near the window bottom and sends Ctrl+A and Ctrl+C. Donald reported the Claude tab freezing with a stray one-line selection (the permission-prompt line " Do you want to proceed?", 24 characters) and said it happens after reading the console. In my log the selections did not line up with the reads to the second, and I never proved the cause. Hardening made in sublime_mcp.py (not committed): record the active view's selection first, refuse to click unless the console panel is really open, restore the selection afterwards; the 13 console-tail tests pass. Detail: .claude/memory/project_ghostshell_phantom_selection_console_read_2026_10_08.md.
- Native dialogs: list_native_windows and dismiss_native_window only enumerate windows of sublime_text.exe. ColorHelper's native colour picker (ChooseColorW, use_os_color_picker=true, a setting I created for the test) raises its "Color" dialog from plugin_host-3.14.exe; it froze Sublime for 169 s, was invisible to those two tools, and every computer-use approval prompt is drawn inside the frozen Sublime window, so it could not be answered. Donald judged it a testing hurdle; nothing was changed in the tools. A fix would enumerate the plugin host's windows too. Do not re-enable the native picker; warn Donald before any test that can open a native modal.
- Other modal dialogs raised during the tests and answered through computer-use or by Donald: RegReplace invalid-regex error, Cargo.sublime-syntax load error after Rust Enhanced was removed, GitHubTools "Please open a file first" (my window command ran with the Claude tab active), UnicodeConverter message, SideBarTools delete confirmation (message text not shown by list_native_windows), phpfmt "Can't find PHP binary".
- Output limits I hit: get_quick_panel without a text filter returned 100 entries (58 KB) on the picker; get_command_palette with arguments outside "args" returned every command; eval_python has a 5 s limit (my own sleeps timed out); sublime.log_commands floods the console with render arguments (600 KB) and sublime.log_input prints every key and typed character Donald presses in Sublime (I left it on for about three hours by mistake; memory only, not on disk, a restart clears it).
- str_replace_based_edit_tool create returns ok for a path whose folder does not exist and opens an unsaved tab; the failure only shows at save time.
- Captured console mode does show Python tracebacks and print output; the visible mode is needed for Sublime's own native lines (for example "Unable to decode ..." and "unexpected rule type ..." syntax errors).
- Cross-package side effects seen while testing: phpfmt's top-level diff_match_patch folder stayed in sys.modules after removal and broke another package's library; ColorHelper's install used the mdpopups library without markdown, pygments and pymdownx on Python 3.14. Always clear a removed package's stale sys.modules entries before the next test.

Also console warnings: version_args, version_re, version_requirement, executable "has no effect", and `get_view_settings()` deprecated. Plugin's split_match still unpacks the old 7-tuple. Test .gd file with bad names, an unnecessary pass and a 119-character line: SublimeLinter panel showed 5 findings (4 errors: variable/constant/function names, 1 warning: unnecessary-pass) with right lines. **Defect (proven against the tool):** the tool itself reports a 6th finding, `gd_test.gd:11:max-line-length:warning: Line is too long. Found 119 characters, maximum allowed is 100`, which never appears in the editor or the panel. Cause from the plugin's regex: `(?P<message>.+?(?P<near>'[^']+'){1}?.*)$` requires a single-quoted token inside every message; the max-line-length message has none, so the line does not match and is dropped (the README even documents the `--max-line-length` setting, which therefore can never show anything). Reproduce: any .gd line over 100 characters. Not filed (his rule: ask first). Draft: "Warnings whose message contains no quoted word are dropped (max-line-length). The tool prints `file:11:max-line-length:warning: Line is too long. Found 119 characters, maximum allowed is 100`; the regex in linter.py requires a `'quoted'` group, so SublimeLinter shows nothing for it. Making the `near` group optional should fix it." Removed both packages (console confirmed), tools\gdscript_formatter recycled, test file deleted, SublimeLinter kept with settings reset to {}.
Addendum (GDScriptFormatterLinter, 2026-10-11 late): issues are disabled on Taffer/GDScript-formatter-linter (mirror); with his "go ahead" the finding was EMAILED to chrish@taffer.ca (subject "GDScript-formatter-linter: max-line-length warnings are not shown"), starting "Claude reports:", with the tested regex fix `(?P<message>(?:.+?(?P<near>'[^']+'))?.*)$` (old pattern fails the max-line-length line, new one matches all three sample lines and keeps `near`). Gmail message id 1a12e47c11d3bd53. No reply expected or checked unless he asks.

## SublimeLinter-contrib-flog (2026-10-11, portable 4200, picker install, tail list) - PARTIAL
v1.0.2 (icnagy; RubyLinter, selector source.ruby, threshold setting 12.0 turns scores above it into errors). Needed Ruby (already installed, 3.4.11) and the `flog` gem (4.9.4 + sexp_processor 4.17.6 + path_expander 2.0.1, installed with `gem install flog --no-document`, `C:\Ruby34-x64\bin` set through SublimeLinter "paths"). Test .rb with a simple and a tangled method: flog by hand prints `55.5: main#tangled   C:/Users/donal/.../flog_test.rb:5-20`. In the portable the panel said "No lint results" and the console warned: `flog reported errors coming from '\Users\donal\AppData\Local\Temp\tmp....rb'. However, reading that file raised: [WinError 3] The system cannot find the path specified`. **Cause proven from the regex:** `\s*(?P<message>[\d\.]+):[^/]+(?P<filename>.+):(?P<line>\d+)-(?P<end_line>\d+)` - `[^/]+` swallows the drive letter of a Windows path, so filename becomes `/Users/donal/...` (checked in Python on the real line); SublimeLinter then resolves it on the current drive. The portable runs from D: while the temp file is on C:, hence the failure. **Not confirmed** whether an installed Sublime on C: (current drive = temp drive) works by luck; no C:-based Sublime was tested (would need the main one or a moved portable), so NOT filed. Candidate fix if confirmed: make the drive optional in the regex (e.g. `(?P<filename>(?:[A-Za-z]:)?[^:]+)`), tested only in principle. Side observation: after SublimeLinter-contrib-todo was removed earlier in the same session, SublimeLinter still listed "todo-linter" among running linters ("Running flog, todo-linter" and "todo-linter cannot locate 'todo-linter'" warnings) until a restart; a removed linter stays registered in SublimeLinter in memory (SublimeLinter/Sublime behaviour, not flog). Removed the linter (console confirmed), uninstalled the three gems (gem list identical to the snapshot taken before), test file deleted, SublimeLinter kept, settings reset to {}.
Addendum (flog, 2026-10-11 late): CONFIRMED and FILED after his rebuke ("you just run into a bug, and do not do what is correct?"). Proof: SublimeLinter's `normalize_filename` (lint/linter.py ~line 1507) only treats a match as the linted file when `normcase(filename) == normcase(temp_file or view file)`; the plugin regex yields a drive-less `/Users/...` that never equals `C:\Users\...`, so on every Windows machine the result is treated as a different file (read from disk, then dropped or attached elsewhere); not specific to the D: portable. Fix tested in Python: `\s*(?P<message>[\d\.]+):\s+\S+\s+(?P<filename>.+):(?P<line>\d+)-(?P<end_line>\d+)` (keeps `C:/...`, `C:\...\a b\t.rb`, Unix paths; ignores the "flog total" and "flog/method average" lines). Filed https://github.com/icnagy/SublimeLinter-contrib-flog/issues/3 (starts "Claude reports:"). Lesson: when a test hits a defect, finish the proof (read the host's source) instead of stopping at "unconfirmed".

**Package Control finding (cause of the stale `installed_packages` entries, now PROVEN):** after this removal the console showed `Package Control: Removed package "Atlas Ragnarok Color Scheme"` and then `Package Control: Error submitting usage information. Operation timed out (errno 12002) ... stats.sublimetext.io/event?...&type=remove`; the entry stayed in User\Package Control.sublime-settings for 28 s and only then vanished. Source (package_manager.py 4.2.8, line ~1927): `remove_package()` calls `update_installed_packages(remove=name, persist=False)`, deletes the folder, then calls `record_usage()` (synchronous `http_get`); the on-disk list was written only after that call ended. Closing Sublime inside that window leaves the entry and the next start reinstalls the package (seen with Selenized and Estomato). FILED https://github.com/sublimehq/package_control/issues/1802 ("Removed package stays in installed_packages on disk until the usage report finishes ..."; the repo is sublimehq/package_control now). Closed with the exit tool after the list was clean; test files deleted.

DEFECT: the package also ships cataracted-dark-theme.sublime-theme, which appears in UI: Select Theme; choosing it breaks the window (menu becomes hamburger, status bar text gone, inactive tab names clipped/invisible, theme picker list unreadable) because the file is a bare rule list with no extends. ## templatejs (syntax for template.js; package repo yanhaijing/template-sublime v0.1.0, created and last pushed Aug 2020; Package Control listing/url points at the template.js library repo) - portable 4200, 2026-10-12
DEFECT: opening a .tmpl file shows the modal error 'Error loading syntax file Packages/templatejs/templatejs.sublime-syntax: Apparent recursion within a with_prototype action: 25000 context sanity limit hit'; status bar says templatejs but every scope is text.plain (same buffer as HTML gives text.html.basic). Cause: with_prototype rule pushes template and the with_prototype re-applies to the pushed context; meta_include_prototype false on template does not help. Proved fix: rewrite with extends: Packages/HTML/HTML.sublime-syntax, version 2, prototype meta_prepend include, as Sublime's own Rails syntax does (needs ST 4075+; package says >=3092): HTML coloured, markers get support.type/keyword.operator/keyword.control/support.function. Filed yanhaijing/template-sublime#1. The captured console does not show core syntax errors; the modal dialog text (list_native_windows) and the get_console visible error hint were how the message was read. Removed (file, list, console); fixed copy and test files recycled; settings identical.

## LaTeXTools with a real TeX distribution (2026-10-13, portable 4200)
LaTeXTools 4.5.16 via palette. Real TeX: MiKTeX 26.5 PORTABLE built with MiKTeX's own miktexsetup_standalone (unsigned; its zip was byte-identical from the CTAN mirror and from miktex.org) into tools\miktex (basic package set 250 MB download, 970 MB installed), MiKTeX bin on PATH only for the launched Sublime; SumatraPDF 3.6.1 portable (signature valid) for the viewer. Worked: install, Package Control messages tab, 'LaTeXTools: Check System' (second run), Traditional Builder compile via latextools_make_pdf (texify, pdflatex, 'No errors. No warnings. [Finished, 1 page written in 1.2s]'), SumatraPDF launched with the sumatra setting in User\LaTeXTools.sublime-settings; the dialog 'Could not find SumatraPDF.exe' appears without it. FINDINGS: LaTeXTools#1717: Check System dies with an uncaught subprocess.TimeoutExpired (biber --version >30 s on first run because MiKTeX installs it on demand), no report; seen once, could not repeat (biber answered in 2 s afterwards); fix (try/except returning None) tested with timeout=1 on the real biber/findtexmf: report is produced. LaTeXTools#1718: with MiKTeX the builder adds texify --quiet, which makes the log use file:line: error style that LaTeXTools' log parser ignores: a failed build prints 'No errors. No warnings. [Build failed!]'; without --quiet the classic '! Undefined control sequence' log is parsed and the build shows 'Errors: a.tex:4: Undefined control sequence near ...'; fix tested (drop --quiet for texify, restart needed). Mistakes/lessons: Build with a variant build system opens a picker (the 'mini-picker' Donald saw for about 45 s was my first plain build command; use latextools_make_pdf or pick the variant), dismiss_native_window needed two calls for the Sumatra dialog, unpacked-copy edits to plugins\builder need a Sublime restart, my long scratch path made TeX wrap the error line and hid the cause for a while (test with a short path). Not tried: TeX Live/latexmk, Basic builder, forward/inverse search, bibliography, snippets/completions. Cleaned: package zip/copy/user settings, tools\miktex, miktex-setup, sumatra, tx_test, scratch recycled; settings restored; Package Control will remove the orphaned library regex at next start.
